title: 2012 HMMT February Algebra Problem 7
statement: Let \(\otimes\) be a binary operation that takes two positive real numbers and returns a positive real number. Suppose further that \(\otimes\) is continuous, commutative \((a \otimes b=b \otimes a)\), distributive across multiplication \((a \otimes(b c)=(a \otimes b)(a \otimes c))\), and that \(2 \otimes 2=4\). Solve the equation \(x \otimes y=x\) for \(y\) in terms of \(x\) for \(x>1\).

solutions.text:
\(y=\sqrt{2}\) We note that \(\left(a \otimes b^{k}\right)=(a \otimes b)^{k}\) for all positive integers \(k\). Then for all rational numbers \(\frac{p}{q}\) we have \(a \otimes b^{\frac{p}{q}}=\left(a \otimes b^{\frac{1}{q}}\right)^{p}=(a \otimes b)^{\frac{p}{q}}\). So by continuity, for all real numbers \(a, b\), it follows that \(2^{a} \otimes 2^{b}=(2 \otimes 2)^{a b}=4^{a b}\). Therefore given positive reals \(x, y\), we have \(x \otimes y=2^{\log _{2}(x)} \otimes 2^{\log _{2}(y)}=\) \(4^{\log _{2}(x) \log _{2}(y)}\).
If \(x=4^{\log _{2}(x) \log _{2}(y)}=2^{2 \log _{2}(x) \log _{2}(y)}\) then \(\log _{2}(x)=2 \log _{2}(x) \log _{2}(y)\) and \(1=2 \log _{2}(y)=\log _{2}\left(y^{2}\right)\). Thus \(y=\sqrt{2}\) regardless of \(x\).
